columns.description: Share of function-call gas paid to the called contract on that day (the developer gas rebate): the newest protocol config read on or before the day, and the first read's 0.3 before 2026-10-28. A change that registry/protocol_upgrades.csv dates to the block holds from the next day, and its own day takes both rates weighted by the time each was in force, as if gas were spread evenly over the day: 0.147 on 2026-11-04, when protocol version 87 set the share to 0 at 11:46:29 UTC.

columns.name: burn_near
columns.description: Gas fees (fct_chain_daily.gas_fee_near) times one minus contract_gas_reward_rate. The rebate came only out of gas burnt executing function calls, so before protocol version 87 the real burn was more than 70% of gas and this is a lower bound; the upper bound is the whole fee, fct_chain_daily.gas_fee_near. The burn can be read straight off the chain only before issuance began on 2020-10-20, when every fall in supply was gas burned: over those 79 days supply fell by 84.8% of gas fees, 124.4 NEAR against this column's 102.7, and the lower bound held on every one of them, which a data test keeps. That share belongs to 2020's mix of transactions and is not applied to later years. From 11:46:29 UTC on 2026-11-04 all gas burns; that day itself is the time-weighted mix.

columns.name: minted_near

It inherits burn_near's lower bound, so before 2026-11-04 the real figure is higher by up to 30% of that day's gas fee, which is small against issuance: 3.36M NEAR of modelled burn against 314.5M minted through 2026-11-08.

description: NEAR's circulating supply per UTC day, built from the chain, from the day transfers were enabled. NEAR defines it as every token not subject to a lockup at that moment. This uses NEAR Explorer's formula: total supply, minus what every lockup contract still locks, minus the balances of lockup.near and contributors.near. Tested against NearBlocks' own lockup job while that ran, NEAR's published schedule, and the contracts' own answers. It does not take out the NEAR Foundation's liquid holding or the protocol treasury, and it counts staked tokens as circulating. See docs/CIRCULATING_SUPPLY.md.

description: NEAR Intents per UTC day, one column per measure. All-route volume and gross fees are revenue.near.org's, which counts confidential routes too; on the few days the page lacks, DefiLlama fills in, and volume_basis and fees_basis say which. Public volume, swaps, accounts, tokens and chains are NearBlocks', which sees public Intents only, so volume_usd minus public_volume_usd is confidential volume. From 2026-11-03 almost all volume settles confidentially, so the public columns describe a small part of Intents. Captured revenue is DefiLlama's. DefiLlama's own volume and fees are not columns here: they count public routes only from 2026-04-01 (volume to 08-31, fees to 09-13), so dq_reconciliation compares them with the page and NearBlocks instead. The fee and revenue columns of the newest days can still change; see is_fee_revenue_provisional.

columns.name: public_volume_usd
columns.description: Public Intents volume per NearBlocks. Starts on 2025-10-29, the oldest day its 365-day window held at the first read. From 2026-11-03 almost all Intents volume settles confidentially, so this fell from about 60% of volume_usd in late October to between 0.4% and 18%; NEAR's own dashboard on Dune shows the same fall. The other public counts fell with it. It comes from another source than volume_usd, NearBlocks' reading of the chain against NEAR's own tally, so while nearly everything was public the two differed by noise: through 2026-04-20 it read above volume_usd on 88 days, by more than 2% on 4 of them and by 7.7% at most (2026-04-18). So volume_usd minus public_volume_usd is not a clean confidential series on such days; floor it at zero. A data test holds it within 10% above volume_usd.

From 2026-02-23, the first day of buybacks (dim_date.is_fee_switch_active), it is the revenue used for buybacks; before, it was held by the treasury. fees_usd minus revenue_usd is what solvers and distribution channels kept; sum that over weeks, because sweeps make single days negative.

columns.description: True while this day's fee and revenue columns can still change, which is until they have been read 3 nights after the day ended: the newest two days of a nightly build. revenue.near.org and DefiLlama publish a day before its data has fully arrived, then rewrite it. The page read $9,319 for 2026-11-03 and $164,920 a night later, and DefiLlama follows a night after the page. Leave these days out of trends and totals. Volume columns are not affected. The number comes from few reads (2026-10-28 to 2026-11-05), and a data test fails if a figure moves in the day's first week after the flag clears. False does not mean final for good: a later rewrite of history would show in dq_revisions.

description: Point in time: tokens and native NEAR per tracked account, per snapshot. This cannot be backfilled, so history starts with the first snapshot. Symbol and decimals come from registry/tokens.csv where a token is listed, then from its contract's ft_metadata, which the nightly job reads for up to 2,000 tokens a night, then from the price list that prices the token (metadata_source says which). A list counts whole tokens with its own decimals, so its price and its decimals belong together, and the lists matched the contract on every token read so far; the test token_decimals_lists_match_contracts fails if that stops. A contract that has answered is final, even with an error, so no list fills in behind it. A token with none of the three keeps empty symbol, amount_token and decimals: nothing is guessed. Earlier snapshots convert too, because the latest answer for a token applies to all of them. value_usd multiplies amount_token by the price read in the same snapshot, joined on token_id from fct_token_prices, which holds the price itself, and value_status says why a row has none. Sum value_usd, never amount_token times a list price: those prices include one that would read $46.5B for one meme token at v2.ref-finance.near. Native NEAR is the RPC view_account balance read the same night where there is one, because FastNear's account state for treasury.near read 47.76 NEAR on every snapshot while the account held about 1.59M.

description: Point in time: one USD price per token per read, chosen from 1Click and Rhea on the token's id, never its symbol. 1Click wins where it has a positive price, because 139 of its 152 tokens carry a market feed's id, while Rhea's list is one DEX's pools. A price of 0 or below on either list counts as no price. Tokens with no positive price on either list have no row. native:near takes wrap.near's price, because one redeems for the other one to one. Most of Rhea's list is stale or thin: 4,309 of the 4,609 tokens on all five reads to 2026-11-05 kept one unchanged price while NEAR moved 11%, and one token reads $1.36 trillion. So read price_date and depth_usd before using a Rhea price.

Rhea gives no time, so this is the first read showing this exact price, digit by digit. Earlier than snapshot_date means the price has not changed since then, and it can never read earlier than Rhea's first read, 2026-11-01.

columns.name: tvl_usd
columns.description: Chain TVL per DefiLlama. DefiLlama can rewrite a chain's history on any night without notice, so no value is ever final and a TVL chart reproduces only at a pin. Its 2026-11-03 read moved 2,079 Ethereum and Solana days back to 2021, by up to 11.4%. Other reads through 2026-11-05 moved at most 8 days by more than 0.01%, and NEAR's series has not moved. See dq_revisions.

columns.name: fees_usd
columns.description: Fees paid to the applications on the chain: DefiLlama's daily total over the protocols it lists there. The chain's own transaction fees are not in it; they are gas_fees_usd. For NEAR most of it is NEAR Intents: $194,787 of $211,521 on 2026-11-08, beside $2,472 of gas, as read on 2026-11-10. DefiLlama also rewrites older days: its 2026-11-04 and 11-05 reads moved 165 and 557 of Solana's days, back to 2025-04-09, by up to 5.6%.

columns.name: revenue_usd

columns.name: gas_fees_usd

First fetched on 2026-11-10, so it is empty in a build pinned before that date. For NEAR it is within 0.2% of NearBlocks' transaction fees at the day's close in every year, from a different indexer (Allium); dq_reconciliation holds the two together. Each series has its own start: NEAR 2020-10-14, Solana 2021-01-17, Aptos 2022-10-18, Avalanche 2022-11-08, Sui 2024-07-01, TON 2024-09-24; Ethereum's starts before this table does.

columns.description: minted_30d_near minus burn_30d_near minus revenue_inflow_30d_near: what the window added to the NEAR outside the revenue wallets.

columns.name: offset_share
columns.description: burn_30d_near plus revenue_inflow_30d_near, over minted_30d_near: the share of issuance that came back. Empty before issuance began on 2020-10-20.

columns.name: gross_inflation_rate
columns.description: minted_30d_near times 365/30, over the window's mean total supply.

columns.name: net_inflation_rate
columns.description: net_issuance_30d_near times 365/30, over the window's mean total supply. Above zero means supply outside the revenue wallets is still growing.

columns.name: nominal_staking_yield_rate
columns.description: Issuance paid to validators and their delegators over the window (minted less the treasury's share), times 365/30, over the window's mean stake. Before pool commission, which the warehouse does not hold. Empty where fewer than five days of the window have a validator reading; the readings are sampled epochs, sparse before 2025-10.

columns.name: real_staking_yield_rate
columns.description: nominal_staking_yield_rate minus gross_inflation_rate: what staking pays beyond the dilution every holder bears.

columns.name: staked_share
columns.description: The window's mean stake over its mean total supply, from the same sampled epochs as the yield.

columns.name: minted_30d_usd
columns.description: The window's issuance at each day's closing price. Empty where a day of the window has no price.

columns.name: revenue_inflow_30d_usd
columns.description: The window's revenue inflows in USD: the sum of fct_revenue_inflows_daily.received_usd.

columns.name: is_burn_lower_bound
columns.description: True while the window holds a day before protocol version 87 (2026-11-04), when part of each gas fee was rebated to contracts and burn_near is a lower bound. From 2026-12-04 every window is exact.

description: The Intents volume at which NEAR's supply would stop growing, under today's issuance and under the end state of HSP-029, at several shares of fees kept. All inputs are measured over the 30 days ending on as_of_date. Revenue is in dollars and issuance in NEAR, so break-even volume rises in step with price_usd and falls in step with fee_rate; a reader can rescale a row to another price or fee rate. The fee rate and the capture rate are held fixed, though both depend on which flows grow.

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.description: The newest day whose Intents fees are settled; every input is the 30 days ending here, and price_usd is this day's close.

columns.name: scenario_id
columns.description: Issuance scenario from registry/issuance_scenarios.csv: current is what the chain minted over the window; hsp029_end_state is 1.6% of supply a year, which has passed its vote but is not in force.

columns.name: capture_case
columns.description: Which capture rate the row assumes: measured, or at_50_pct, at_70_pct, at_100_pct.

columns.name: issuance_near_per_day
columns.description: NEAR issued per day in the scenario.

columns.name: burn_near_per_day
columns.description: NEAR burned as gas per day over the window, held fixed across scenarios.

columns.name: price_usd
columns.description: NEAR's close on as_of_date, from fct_market_daily.

columns.name: fee_rate
columns.description: Intents fees over Intents volume across the window.

columns.name: capture_rate
columns.description: Share of Intents fees that reaches the revenue wallets: the window's revenue over fees for the measured case, else the case's rate.

columns.name: volume_usd_per_day
columns.description: Mean daily all-route Intents volume over the window.

columns.name: breakeven_volume_usd_per_day
columns.description: Daily Intents volume at which the NEAR bought with captured fees equals issuance less burn: (issuance_near_per_day - burn_near_per_day) x price_usd / (fee_rate x capture_rate).

columns.name: breakeven_volume_multiple
columns.description: breakeven_volume_usd_per_day over volume_usd_per_day: how many times today's volume it would take.

columns.name: net_inflation_rate_at_current_volume
columns.description: What net inflation would be in the scenario at today's volume: issuance less burn less the NEAR that volume_usd_per_day x fee_rate x capture_rate buys, times 365, over mean supply.

description: NEAR's Intents revenue per month, split into what makes it: volume, the fee rate charged on it, and the share of fees NEAR keeps. revenue_usd = volume_usd x fee_rate x capture_rate, so a month's change splits exactly into three log effects. Volume and fees are NEAR's own all-route series and revenue is what reached the wallets, which are swept in lumps, so a month is the shortest span on which capture means anything. Days whose fees can still change are left out, so the newest month is short.

columns.name: month_start
columns.description: First day of the month.

columns.name: days_counted
columns.description: Days of the month with settled figures.

columns.name: is_month_complete
columns.description: True when every day of the month is counted. The newest month is not.

columns.name: volume_usd
columns.description: All-route Intents volume over the counted days.

columns.name: fees_usd
columns.description: Intents fees over the counted days. Fee data begins in May 2025.

columns.name: revenue_usd
columns.description: Revenue that reached NEAR's wallets over the counted days.

columns.name: fee_rate
columns.description: fees_usd over volume_usd, on the days that have fees.

columns.name: capture_rate
columns.description: revenue_usd over fees_usd: the share of fees NEAR keeps. The rest stays with distribution partners, solvers and front ends.

columns.name: net_take_rate
columns.description: revenue_usd over volume_usd: what NEAR keeps per dollar swapped.

columns.name: confidential_volume_share
columns.description: One minus public volume over all-route volume, on the days that have a public figure, with public volume capped at all-route volume day by day because the two come from different sources. Empty before public volume is held.

columns.name: revenue_log_change
columns.description: Change in the natural log of revenue per day from the month before. It equals the sum of the three effects. Empty unless both months are complete, have fees on every day and at least $1,000 of revenue; the wallets' first months held test transfers.

columns.name: volume_log_effect
columns.description: The part of revenue_log_change from volume per day.

columns.name: fee_rate_log_effect
columns.description: The part of revenue_log_change from the fee rate.

columns.name: capture_log_effect
columns.description: The part of revenue_log_change from the capture rate.

description: What each 1Click distribution channel brought in per month: finished volume, the app fees charged on it, and the fee rate that implies. It shows who prices NEAR's fee base. 1Click is one part of NEAR Intents (27% to 45% of volume in 2026) and only its unbroken daily run is used. App fees are what a channel adds for itself or passes on; they are not NEAR's revenue.

columns.name: month_start
columns.description: First day of the month.

columns.name: referral
columns.description: The channel, as the integrator names itself to 1Click. (none) is every swap sent without a name, a bucket and not one channel.

columns.name: is_month_complete
columns.description: True when the daily run covers every day of the month.

columns.name: finished_swaps
columns.description: Swaps that finished.

columns.name: refunded_swaps
columns.description: Swaps that were refunded.

columns.name: refunded_share
columns.description: refunded_swaps over finished plus refunded swaps.

columns.name: volume_usd
columns.description: USD paid in on finished swaps.

columns.name: app_fee_usd
columns.description: App fees on finished swaps.

columns.name: app_fee_rate
columns.description: app_fee_usd over volume_usd. 0.0082 is 82 basis points.

columns.name: share_of_volume
columns.description: The channel's share of the month's finished 1Click volume.

columns.name: share_of_fees
columns.description: The channel's share of the month's 1Click app fees.

columns.name: fee_rank
columns.description: Rank within the month by app fees, 1 the largest.

description: How concentrated NEAR Intents is, per month, along four cuts: 1Click channels by volume and by fees, and public volume by blockchain and by asset. covered_share_of_volume says how much of all-route volume a cut can see: 1Click is a minority of volume, and the public cuts fell below a fifth once settlement went confidential on 2026-11-03.

columns.name: month_start
columns.description: First day of the month.

columns.name: dimension
columns.description: The cut: channel_volume and channel_fees (1Click, finished swaps of the daily run), chain_volume and asset_volume (public Intents per NearBlocks).

columns.name: is_month_complete
columns.description: True when the cut's source has every day of the month.

columns.name: members
columns.description: Channels, blockchains or assets with a positive amount in the month. For channels, (none) counts as one.

columns.name: total_usd
columns.description: The month's amount across all members: volume, or app fees for channel_fees.

columns.name: hhi
columns.description: Herfindahl index: the sum of squared shares. 1 is a single member; 1 over the number of members is an even split.

columns.name: top_1_share
columns.description: Share of the largest member.

columns.name: top_3_share
columns.description: Share of the three largest members.

columns.name: top_10_share
columns.description: Share of the ten largest members.

columns.name: top_member
columns.description: The largest member.

columns.name: covered_share_of_volume
columns.description: total_usd over the month's all-route Intents volume, for the three volume cuts: how much of Intents the cut sees. Empty for channel_fees.

description: Market cap over a year of income, for NEAR and six peers, on five ideas of income, one row each because the choice of basis moves NEAR's rank more than anything else. gas_fees is what users paid the chain itself; app_fees what they paid applications on it; all_fees the two together; app_revenue the part of app fees the applications or their tokens keep, which does not go to the chain's own token; holder_revenue, for NEAR only, is gas burned plus NEAR received by the revenue wallets. A year of income is the trailing 30 days times 365/30. Market caps are not on one definition across chains: read fct_peer_daily.market_cap_basis before comparing.

columns.name: date_day
columns.description: Last day of the 30-day window, a UTC calendar day.

columns.name: chain_id
columns.description: Chain identifier from registry/peers.csv.

columns.name: basis
columns.description: Which income the multiple uses: gas_fees, app_fees, all_fees, app_revenue or holder_revenue.

columns.name: basis_30d_usd
columns.description: The basis summed over the 30 days ending on date_day. A window with a missing day has no row.

columns.name: multiple
columns.description: fct_peer_daily.market_cap_usd on date_day over basis_30d_usd times 365/30.

columns.name: is_provisional
columns.description: fct_peer_daily.is_fee_revenue_provisional for the day: true on the newest two days, whose fees and revenue can still change.

description: Transactions with the known batch streams taken out, so usage can be read across the break of 2026-04-02 (docs/USAGE_BREAK_2026-04-02.md), and with the Sweat relayer taken out as well, since Sweat Wallet ends on 2026-12-30. The streams are counted from NearBlocks' per-account statistics, which reach back 365 active days from their first read, so the table starts where the Kai-Ching accounts' statistics do and the Sweat columns start later. A transaction that touches two of the stream accounts is counted in both, so the series without them is a floor.

columns.name: date_day
columns.description: UTC calendar day.

columns.name: batch_stream_txns
columns.description: Transactions involving hotwallet.kaiching, users.kaiching or sweat-migration.near: the fixed daily batch that stopped on 2026-04-01 and the three-week key migration that ended on 2026-04-02.

columns.name: sweat_relayer_txns
columns.description: Transactions involving sweat-relayer.near. Empty before 2025-11-01, where its statistics begin.

columns.name: txns_ex_batch_streams
columns.description: fct_chain_daily.txns minus batch_stream_txns.

columns.name: txns_ex_batch_streams_and_sweat
columns.description: txns_ex_batch_streams minus sweat_relayer_txns: roughly what remains once Sweat Wallet has ended.

columns.name: sweat_share_of_txns_ex_batch_streams
columns.description: sweat_relayer_txns over txns_ex_batch_streams.

columns.name: txn_fee_usd
columns.description: fct_chain_daily.txn_fee_near at the day's closing price.

columns.name: txn_fee_per_txn_near
columns.description: fct_chain_daily.txn_fee_near over all of the day's transactions, batch streams included.

columns.name: sweat_gas_burn_share
columns.description: Share of the gas burnt in the day's sampled blocks whose receiver is labelled Sweat Economy, from fct_receiver_sample_daily. An estimate from a sample: 24 blocks a day before 2026-10-30 and 96 since, so read it over a week or more. Empty before the sample begins.

columns.name: is_before_usage_break
columns.description: True before 2026-04-03. Raw transaction and account counts are not comparable across that date; the columns here without the streams are.

description: The Bitwise NEAR ETF's flows against what the chain issued and what the revenue wallets took in, from the fund's first day, one row per trading day. The seed baskets of 2026-09-28 are left out of the flow. A creation is NEAR delivered to the trust, which need not have been bought on the market that day, and redemptions reverse it. Only this one fund is tracked.

columns.name: date_day
columns.description: Trading day.

columns.name: cumulative_flow_near
columns.description: Running sum of fct_etf_nrr_daily.flow_near since the fund's first day, without the seed baskets.

columns.name: cumulative_minted_near
columns.description: NEAR the chain issued from the fund's first day through this day, every calendar day counted.

columns.name: cumulative_revenue_inflow_near
columns.description: NEAR the revenue wallets received over the same days.

columns.name: cumulative_flow_to_issuance_ratio
columns.description: cumulative_flow_near over cumulative_minted_near: how many times the chain's issuance the fund has taken in since it opened.

columns.name: flow_to_issuance_ratio
columns.description: The day's fund flow in NEAR over the NEAR issued that day. Issuance arrives per epoch, so read single days loosely.

columns.name: flow_share_of_spot_volume
columns.description: The day's fund flow in USD over NEAR's reported spot volume that day; negative on a day of net redemptions.

description: How current each dataset is, relative to the newest snapshot the build can see, and whether that is too old. Covers the daily series and the datasets read as a snapshot each night. A dataset that falls further behind than its limit is stale, and the data test no_dataset_is_stale then fails, so a source that stops arriving is noticed.

columns.name: model

columns.name: cadence

columns.description: Newest day of data. For a snapshot dataset, the day of its newest read.

columns.name: as_of
columns.description: Newest snapshot across all datasets.

columns.name: days_behind
columns.description: Days between latest_data_day and as_of. A daily series normally reads 1, because the newest full day is yesterday.

columns.name: max_days_behind
